assumptions: S origin is placed at the geometric center of the 12U envelope; CoM is assumed near-center (Y=Z=0) but not yet computed — CoM offset and T_SB are TBD per SSOT §4.

Envelope taken as the nominal 12U (2x2x3) form: 340.5 mm (X) x 226.3 mm (Y) x 226.3 mm (Z). Exact CDS Appendix B dims are unverified (drawing-text parse failed, doc §1 limitation) and must be manually reviewed before CAD.

The 340.5 mm long axis is aligned with +X_S (rear service bay -> front task bay = target-approach). Three bays each 113.5 mm (1U) deep partition the body along X: rear [-170.25,-56.75], mid [-56.75,56.75], front [56.75,170.25]. Bay boxes share the full 226.3x226.3 cross-section and union into one monolithic body; internal bulkheads not modeled.

target_mass_kg = 24.0 kg adopted as the CDS Rev14.1 Table 1 12U max-mass reference, used as a design target for the display servicer (confidence low). Builder sizes effective density to hit it. Internal components (OBC/C&DH, EPS/PMAD, battery, reaction-wheel set, IMU) are lumped into the body mass, not modeled as separate outer geometry (they do not change the external envelope).

Robot mount face M = outer datum of a 140x140x15 mm adapter flange centered on the +X front face; M origin [185.25,0,0] mm, outward normal +X_S. Positioned at Y=Z=0 to lie on the CoM lateral projection (req 12U-LR-01) and clear of camera/panels/antenna (req 12U-LR-02).

Camera modeled as a Ø50 x 40 mm cylinder mounted on the front face, offset +80 mm in +Z above the arm mount, boresight +X and near-coaxial with the robot workspace (baseline §4 front-task-face C-over-B); it does not conflict with the mount or occlude when the arm is folded (req 12U-LR-04).

Solar panels modeled as two 227x200x6 mm flat plates deployed on ±Y with Z-normal, spanning only the rear+mid bays (X from -170.25 to +56.75) so they clear the forward robot workspace and camera FOV cone (baseline §2 side deployables). Deployed state assumed; stowed envelope TBD.

Propulsion placeholder = Ø90 x 60 mm cylinder on the -X rear face (nozzle, axis +X, protruding rearward). Antenna placeholder = Ø30 x 50 mm cylinder on the rear-bay +Z face. Both are isolated from the front-end robot workspace and the panels (baseline §2 rear service bay; req in reference-inputs §2).

No fillets, holes, rails, or -Z 'tuna-can' extra volume are modeled; rail contact zones and the -Z extra volume are intentionally left free per CDS. Block model = simple boxes + cylinders unioned only.
Grasp/marker points and tumble axis are N/A for the servicer (they belong to target/debris models); left empty/null.
Reference deployment system assumed rail-reference (baseline §3), pending Appendix B manual review.

Geometry only; inertia is self-defined downstream. No OreSat/PyCubed/BIRDS CAD is copied or renamed — external open assets informed only sub-system stacking/interface ideas per mapping doc §1 (whole-servicer geometry is original, risk RA-001).

mount_face_M.note: Frame M = arm mounting-face / reBot URDF base = adapter flange outer-surface datum. +Z_M = mount-face normal = +X_S (arm reach direction); +X_M (main bolt array) aligned with +Z_S. T_SM = S->M to be read off CAD once the flange bolt pattern is fixed (per coordinate SSOT, this is the mechanical-to-dynamics bridge, old T_SB).

keepout.arm_workspace: Forward hemisphere about +X_S emanating from mount_face_M; solar panels held behind x=+100 mm to stay clear (6U-LR-05).
keepout.rail_contact_surface: CDS Rev14 rail / contact-surface keepout on the deployer-rail edges is TBD pending manual dimension review; not modeled at block-model level.

assumptions: Frame S origin = geometric center of the 6U envelope (100x226.3x366 mm); reconciliation with CoM is deferred to the mass-inertia budget (T_SB S->B offset left TBD).

Axis mapping (documented, not from a fixed drawing): long 366 mm = X_S (rear service bay -> front task bay / approach axis); 100 mm = Y_S (right solar-panel side); 226.3 mm = Z_S (up). Consistent with the CDS Rev14 6U envelope.

The 'single body' is represented as three equal-length X-partitioned bays of 122 mm each (rear_bay, mid_bus_bay, front_task_bay) that sum to the full envelope with zero overlap; no detailed internal packaging (OBC/EPS/battery/RW/IMU are notional occupants of mid_bus_bay, comms/propulsion/interface of rear_bay).

Arm mount = frame M on the +X front task face: M origin at flange outer surface [191,0,0] mm in S; mount-face normal +Z_M = +X_S = [1,0,0] (arm reaches forward); +X_M (main bolt array) aligned with +Z_S. T_SM to be exported/reviewed with the adapter model, not guessed post-CAD.
Camera placeholder co-located on the front task face, offset +50 mm in Z above the arm axis to keep the FOV near-coaxial with the arm capture workspace (6U-LR-02); optical boresight assumed = +X_S.

Two side solar panels modeled as thin (6 mm) body-mounted plates flush on the +/-Y faces, spanning X in [-160,+100] mm to stay clear of the forward arm workspace hemisphere (6U-LR-05). This is a stowed / body-mounted representation only; deployed envelope, hinge line and deployment mechanism are NOT modeled and will change the collision envelope.

Rear propulsion/interface represented by one small nozzle cylinder (r=15, L=30 mm) on -X; individual comms antennas, connectors, harness exits and ground-support interfaces are not modeled (placeholder volume only).
Flange, camera, nozzle and panels are simple geometric placeholders per block-model rules: boxes + cylinders unioned, NO fillets/holes/fasteners/manufacturing detail.

Mass/CoM/inertia are self-defined (RA-003): target_mass_kg = 9.0 kg is a v0 STATED ASSUMPTION, chosen to be lighter than the 12U variant and consistent with ~1100 kg/m^3 effective density over the ~8.3 L envelope; it is NOT a measured value. Inertia tensor to be derived by the deterministic builder / mass-inertia budget about a stated reference point. Confidence: low.

No external CAD geometry is imported: no full-servicer CAD exists (RA-001). Open assets (OreSat, UPSat, OSSAT/KISPE, bac-hardware) informed only subsystem stacking/panel-interconnect concepts; all geometry here is self-authored.
Units are millimeters; all frames right-handed; every primitive is placed by center_offset_mm from the S origin.

Frame T per coordinate_frame_definition_v0 SSOT: right-handed; origin at main-body geometric center; +X_T toward primary grasp interface / servicer approach; +Z_T toward panel-deploy normal; +Y_T completes RH. CoM differs from origin and is recorded separately (features.com_offset_mm).

Chose 12U class over 6U for v0; body simplified to a 340 x 226 x 226 mm box (long axis along X_T) from the CDS 12U envelope. These are v0 PLACEHOLDERS, not verified Appendix B dimensions (12U outer dims flagged manual_review_required, APPB-004).

Agena-like cylindrical section modeled as a launch-adapter / separation-ring stub: radius 100mm (~8-inch/203mm sep-ring class), length 120mm, protruding from the +X body face and unioned to it; geometry informed by NASA-3D Agena only, NO inertia inherited.

Solar panels modeled as two deployable flat stub plates (300 x 200 x 12 mm) along +/-Y, one plate per side, rooted at the body Y faces (y=+/-213 center so root touches +/-113 face); hinge/yoke abstracted to a point; panels are fragile keepout, not a default grasp target.
Antenna modeled as a single slender monopole rod (radius 6mm, length 200mm) along +Z rooted on the top face; abstracts a VHF/UHF whip; slender keepout, not a grasp target.
Mass self-defined at 22.0 kg (~12U upper-mass class ~2 kg/U plus adapter and panels); NOT measured; deterministic builder sizes an effective uniform density to hit this target. confidence low.
Inertia is self-defined downstream and NEVER claimed as measured (risk RA-003 / R-014); this spec provides geometry + mass target only, no inertia tensor asserted here.
CoM assumed offset +40mm along +X_T toward the denser adapter/propulsion end; low confidence, to be replaced by the mass-inertia CSV after component assignment.

Primary grasp = rigid launch-adapter ring at the far +X face of the adapter cylinder (approach along +X_T); secondary grasp = solar-panel structural yoke/root at the +/-Y body faces; the panel laminate itself is explicitly forbidden as a grasp surface.

AprilTag markers self-placed on the servicer-facing +X body face (clear of the adapter-cylinder footprint) and on the +Z top face; IDs and 60mm size are placeholders; markers denote demonstration/perception NARRATIVE only, no completed perception claimed.
Non-cooperative failed satellite assumed slowly tumbling; nominal tumble axis self-defined about +Z_T at ~2-5 deg/s placeholder rate, to be finalized by the Stage 2 scenario matrix; low confidence.

Block model only: boxes + cylinders unioned, all primitives mutually touching/overlapping for a single solid; NO fillets, holes, thin-wall, or mechanism detail; grasp/marker/keepout/tumble entries are annotation metadata, not solid geometry.
All dimensions in millimeters; center_offset_mm is measured from the frame T origin.

assumptions: No manufacturing/measured CAD of a cylindrical upper-stage/adapter debris exists in the asset pool (gap RA-003); this is an ORIGINAL simplified block model, not copied from any open asset. Tsinghua space_robot debris URDF is license-gate D and explicitly NOT used.

Representative envelope chosen: body Ø1200 mm x 2000 mm long = a 'small spent upper-stage / large payload-adapter shell segment' scale, not tied to any specific vehicle (Agena-class ~1.5 m dia noted only as an upper bound reference).

True structure is a thin-walled hollow shell; here it is modeled as solid boxes+cylinders. Inertia is SELF-DEFINED via effective density (builder sizes density to hit target_mass_kg), never claimed as measured (RA-003 / R-014).

target_mass_kg = 150 kg is a STATED ASSUMPTION for a depleted/empty thin-wall aluminum shell of this envelope (lateral+cap area ~9.8 m^2 x ~3 mm Al ~= 80 kg shell + rings/nozzle/residual ~= 150 kg); confidence LOW.
+Z_D = nominal tumble/symmetry axis per SSOT; real debris precesses/nutates and may flat-spin - Z_D is the nominal spin/principal axis only.
Tumble-rate magnitude taken as ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE context from MMT/RoBo6/LCDC light-curve data for Stage-2 angular-rate IC; it informs dynamics, NOT geometry.
Non-cooperative target: no standard servicing/mount interface, so mount_face_M (frame M) is N/A; grasp is on native structure (end rings / reinforced band), never on a defined docking port.
Grasp region = the two proud end rings (rim/ring), the stiffest features; smooth thin cylindrical shell wall is keepout (crush risk).
Aft nozzle stub added to represent a spent engine bell (simplified as a plain cylinder); aft region flagged keepout as fragile / possible residual propellant.

AprilTag/marker features are NOT debris-native - the +X_D shell bracket plate and the flat forward end-cap are provided as CANDIDATE marker locations for the servicer scenario; real debris carries no cooperative marker.
Reinforcement rib ring at z=+300 is a nominal stiffener placeholder (jiagou jin / flange); its exact location is assumed.

D origin placed at the body-cylinder axis mid-point per SSOT; geometric center assumed ~= CoM for the symmetric shell. The nozzle biases CoM slightly toward -Z; this small offset is ignored at v0 (record separately when inertia is estimated).
+X_D chosen as the nominal servicer approach / marker-visible direction (analogous to the +X_T convention in target_models_requirements).
All dimensions in millimeters; primitives are boxes + cylinders only, unioned; no fillets, holes, wall thickness, or manufacturing detail.
